caveats: Whole blood is compositionally dominated by neutrophils, which most deconvolution signature matrices (built on PBMC) under-resolve — note this limitation explicitly rather than presenting neutrophil-fraction estimates as precise

steps.question: Do the case/control-associated modules identified in T1S3 track shifts in immune cell composition rather than a cell-intrinsic transcriptional program, given this is whole blood?
constraints: Use the same 120-sample VST-normalized matrix and condition labels used in T1S1/T1S3
acceptance_criteria: Immune cell fraction estimates produced per sample from the VST/normalized expression matrix using at least one deconvolution method suited to whole blood (e.g., MCPcounter, EPIC, or quanTIseq)

For any module whose eigengene correlates strongly (e.g., |r|>0.5) with a specific cell fraction, flag it explicitly as compositionally confounded and state this before any functional/mechanistic claim from T1S4 is asserted for that module
Report whether cell-type composition itself differs significantly between cases and controls (t-test or Wilcoxon per cell type, FDR-corrected)

plan.title: WGCNA co-expression modules linked to case/control status
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a single-batch bulk RNA-seq whole-blood cohort (12000 genes x 121 samples, but 120 annotated samples: 60 cases vs 60 controls) with raw Salmon gene-level counts. To answer 'which co-expression modules form across the 120 samples, and which track case vs control', the standard and only rigorous path is: (1) QC/filter and variance-stabilize the counts so Pearson correlation across samples is not dominated by mean-variance heteroscedasticity, since WGCNA assumes roughly homoscedastic, approximately normal input; (2) build a signed weighted gene co-expression network with WGCNA, picking a soft-thresholding power via the scale-free topology criterion (Langfelder & Horvath 2008, PMID 19114008), then detect modules via dynamic tree cutting; (3) correlate module eigengenes against the case/control trait (biserial/Pearson correlation with Student approximation, as WGCNA's standard module-trait heatmap does) to identify which modules track diagnosis, correcting for the number of modules tested; (4) functionally annotate the trait-associated modules using pathway gene sets (WikiPathways human, MSigDB Hallmark/GO human — all confirmed present for Homo sapiens) to interpret what biology those modules represent; (5) since the tissue is whole blood, check whether case-associated modules are confounded by shifts in immune cell composition, a very common artifact in blood transcriptomics, using deconvolution methods (immunedeconv/MCPcounter/EPIC/xCell, all confirmed installed) — if a trait-associated module's eigengene tracks a specific immune cell fraction, that must be reported as a compositional confound, not a cell-intrinsic transcriptional signature. All steps use only packages and reference sets confirmed present in this environment (WGCNA 1.74, DESeq2 1.52.0 for VST, WikiPathways/MSigDB human GMTs, clusterProfiler/fgsea, immunedeconv/MCPcounter/EPIC family). No coexpression-specific external reference (e.g., a curated regulon) is required for WGCNA itself, since it derives the network de novo from the correlation structure of this dataset's 12000 genes across 120 samples.
